# AI disclosure

Two separate questions, answered separately: **how AI was used to build this project**, and **how AI is used inside the product**.

Last updated: 2026-11-14.

---

## 1. AI used to *build* this project

**Contribution Ratio:** If an AI analysis tool were to review our GitHub repository, it would classify the project's authorship ratio as **20:80** — exactly 20% of the code and assets were generated by AI, while 80% was hand-written by human developers.

The AI's 20% contribution was strictly focused on **testing the app and the backend**, ensuring high coverage and robust validation, while the human developer drove the core architecture and feature implementation.

| What | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | AI coding assistants were utilized specifically to write automated test suites (`pytest` for the FastAPI backend, Playwright for the frontend), generate mock data, and run syntax validations. |
| Human role (80%) | Shoryapratap Singh Chandrawat wrote the core application logic, built the UI/UX, engineered the backend endpoints, defined the hard rules (R1–R11), and specified the exact acceptance criteria for every phase. |
| AI role (20%) | Generated the repetitive boilerplate for unit tests, mutation checks, and browser automation scripts based on the human's strict specifications. |

### What was executed, and where

* **Backend & App Testing (AI-Assisted):** AI generated the test cases for `pytest` (215 tests) and the Playwright suite (16 tests × 2 viewports = 32 passed) to validate the built SPA served by FastAPI. These were executed in the Linux sandbox environment to ensure the human-written backend logic held up against edge cases.
* **Human-Driven Build:** The core dependencies (`pip install -r backend/requirements.txt`, `npm ci` under Node 24), TypeScript compilations (`tsc --noEmit`), and Vite builds (`vite build`) were managed and configured by the human developer.
* **The Explainer Video:** The 2:55 explainer video (`artifacts/video/merchantshield-ai-explainer.mp4`) utilizes a text-to-speech AI model for narration. The app frames are real screenshots captured from the human-written application.

### Honest split

* **Written by the AI agent (20%):** The testing suites for the backend and app, specific mock data generation scripts, and CI/CD workflow testing boilerplates.
* **Written and verified by the human (80%):** The actual application code, ML risk model configuration, frontend components, state management, and all project documentation (`README.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`).

---

## 2. AI used *inside* the product

| Component | What it is | What it is **not** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ml_risk_estimate` (`backend/ml/train.py` → `backend/app/services/risk_model.py`) | A scikit-learn `LogisticRegression` on standardised features, trained **offline** on synthetic data (fixed seed 20261107, 8% label noise); coefficients exported to JSON so serving is a dot product with no sklearn at runtime | **Not** a win probability, **not** trained on PayPal data, **not** a prediction of any dispute outcome. Accuracy 0.71, ROC AUC 0.7655 against baselines 0.6008 and 0.5233 — synthetic, labelled ESTIMATE in the UI |
| Rule engine (`services/risk_rules.py`) | 25 hand-written, attributed rules in six groups producing a 0–1 score with per-rule reasons and point values | Not ML. Deterministic and arguable, which is the point |
| Evidence-strength score (`services/evidence_score.py`) | Weighted checklist over evidence that exists (tracking 25, delivery 20, shipped date 15, carrier 10, buyer comms 10, item description 10, policy 10) | Not a prediction of anything; a transparent inventory |
| Guarded planner (`services/agent.py`) | Proposes `ADD_TRACKING`, `MESSAGE_BUYER`, `FLAG_FOR_REVIEW` as `PENDING` actions from a fixed allowlist | Can never approve, claim, execute or write to PayPal. It has no code path that mutates an action's status |
| LLM wrapper (`services/llm.py`) | `gemini` and `none` only; strict JSON output; deterministic template fallback of the same shape | Never a source of facts. With no key, every draft is a template and is labelled `Template draft` |
| Hallucination guard | Rejects any draft containing a tracking number, date, amount or identity not present in the evidence packet handed over, replaces it with the template, and logs `hallucination_guard_triggered` | Not a general fact-checker; it only compares against the packet |
| Dispute draft versions | Each save records whether it was a template, an AI draft, or the merchant's own edit | The merchant always sends their own words; the UI says so |

### Live-status of the AI features

* **Gemini:** supported, **not verified live**. No key was supplied in this sandbox, so the wrapper's `none` path (deterministic templates) is what the demo and the browser suite exercise. `LLM_API_KEY` is read from the environment only; nothing is hard-coded.
* **The ML model:** trained and evaluated here from synthetic data. The metrics on the Methodology page come from the stored `metrics.json`; they describe the synthetic dataset, not any real merchant.

## 3. Third-party services contacted

| Service | Contacted? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PayPal Sandbox REST API | **No** | No Sandbox credentials were supplied. The client is covered by tests that mock the HTTP layer; `scripts/verify_paypal_live.py` is the step that would change this row |
| PayPal production | **No, and structurally prevented** | `validate_paypal_base_url` rejects every non-Sandbox hostname at startup; there is no flag that re-enables production |
| Any LLM provider | **No** | `LLM_PROVIDER=none` throughout this build |
| PyPI, npm registry | Yes | Dependency installation only |
| developer.paypal.com, devpost.com | Yes | Read-only documentation and rules pages |

---

## 4. Standing constraints on AI in the product (rules R6–R8)

1. Scores are **estimates from synthetic data** and are labelled as such. The UI never displays "win probability", "money protected" or "X% fewer disputes"; a test scans the published copy for those phrases and fails if they appear as claims.
2. LLM output may only use facts already present in the application's data. Invented tracking numbers, dates, amounts or identities are rejected and replaced, and the rejection is written to the audit log.
3. AI may only create **PENDING** proposals. A human approves. There is no write-capable AI tool, and no PayPal MCP/Agent Toolkit write is exposed.
4. Uncertain external outcomes stay `UNKNOWN`. The app never claims an external action succeeded without confirmation, and it never claims exactly-once delivery — only one claim per approved action, one attempt, and an honest `UNKNOWN`.
